principalConclusion: ARA uses a provider-independent local-first hybrid architecture: strict TypeScript domain/application packages; React/Vite PWA client; IndexedDB local projection/outbox; Service Worker/Cache API offline shell; PostgreSQL connected metadata/relations/policies; S3-compatible immutable artifacts; OIDC identity; revision/operation-log sync; bounded MCP gateway; optional segregated research data plane.
keyConstraints: Domain is independent from Supabase and physical schemas.
Personal baseline has no mandatory account, sync, LLM or event store.
Immutable domain versions are not physical object-store version IDs.
No CRDT or semantic auto-merge in v1.
Supabase is a candidate managed adapter; self-hosted uses conformant replaceable services.
Architecture conformance must pass managed and self-hosted profiles.

Issue8: Use PWA/offline constraints, capability profiles, conflict/failure states and role/policy boundaries in every journey.
Do not expose database/storage internals; expose versions, consequences, sync and capability states.
Issue9: Create TypeScript monorepo/PWA/service/API/storage/sync/MCP release slices and enforce conformance/quality budgets.
Branch protection and CI must be enabled before product implementation.
